title: Render layer effects (drop shadow) in vector PDF export or record them truthfully
outcome: A document whose layers carry a drop shadow exports to vector PDF with the shadow visibly rendered and matching the canvas within tolerance - or, if a truthful vector approximation is impossible for a given effect, the export report records a per-layer rasterFallback or note so the PDF never silently differs from the canvas. VIRO-0015's export corpus pins are updated to the new behavior and its effects parity test flips from documents-the-defect to proves-the-fix.
before: VIRO-0015 export corpus finding (verified 2026-08-28, candidate 3cba4ab, verifier PASS): the effects-layer document's PDF census + report pins are byte-identical to the unshadowed control (corpus parity test), while its compositor PNG fingerprint differs - the canvas paints the drop shadow the vector PDF silently drops. src/document/types.ts claims effects are rendered 'by the exporter'; grep over src/export/ shows zero effects handling. No report note records the divergence. Behavior pinned as current by tests/export-corpus.* on merged main.
after: Drop shadows render in vector PDF output (CanvasKit-consistent blur/offset within tolerance, proven by rendered-PDF pixel comparison against canvas captures), and any effect that cannot be truthfully vectorized produces an explicit report entry. The corpus effects pins are updated and the parity test asserts canvas/PDF shadow parity.
acceptance: A document with one drop-shadowed layer exports to vector PDF whose pdf.js render shows the shadow; rendered-PDF pixels compare against the canvas capture within a stated tolerance (artifact-level proof, not serialization success).
The effects corpus parity test flips: effects-layer PDF no longer byte-matches the unshadowed control; updated pins committed with the fix.
Any non-vectorizable effect path records an explicit rasterFallbacks entry or report note (never silent).
All other corpus pins unchanged or updated only where the shadow legitimately alters output; compound + text + font suites stay green.
npx tsc --noEmit, corpus + new tests, npm run test:chrome and npm run build pass.
evidence: pdf.js rendered-PDF vs canvas pixel comparison (shadow present, tolerance stated)
Updated corpus pins + flipped parity test

builder.notes: Claimable immediately: src/export lease free since VIRO-0015 reconciled.

critic.notes: Exported output is user-visible; critic compares canvas vs PDF renders.

delta.before: Canvas paints drop shadows the vector PDF silently drops; report says nothing.
delta.after: Shadows render in PDF (or are truthfully reported), corpus pins prove parity.

delta.new_debt: Outer glow / stroke effects in PDF may follow in a later packet if vectorization is non-trivial; shadow first.
